incident.title: Which of the following is the true definition of the term _modem_?
incident.question: Which of the following is the true definition of the term _modem_?
choices: A device that connects a computer to the Public Switched Telephone Network (PSTN)
A device that connects a Local Area Network (LAN) to the Internet
A device that converts analog signals to digital signals and back again
A device that connects a Local Area Network (LAN) to a Wide Area Network (WAN)

test_cases.expected_root_cause: A device that converts analog signals to digital signals and back again
test_cases.solution: A modem (modulator/demodulator) is any device that converts analog signals to digital signals and digital signals back to analog signals. The digital device does not have to be a computer, and the analog device does not have to be the PSTN. There are many devices that are incorrectly referred to as modems, such as devices that connect a digital LAN to a digital WAN or all-digital devices that connect computers to the Internet
acceptable_answers: a device that converts analog signals to digital signals and back again

incident.title: What is the protocol of choice for network device access control?
incident.question: What is the protocol of choice for network device access control?
topics: Network Device Access Control and Infrastructure Security

test_cases.solution: TACACS+ is preferred for device access control because it can individually authorize every command that a user tries to execute after logging in to a device. In contrast, RADIUS requires those commands to be sent in the initial authentication response, and because there could be thousands of CLI command combinations, a large authorization result list could trigger memory exhaustion on the network device

incident.title: You are testing a twisted-pair cable run using a tone generator and locator. When you apply the tone generator to a particular pin at one end of the c
incident.question: You are testing a twisted-pair cable run using a tone generator and locator. When you apply the tone generator to a particular pin at one end of the cable, you detect a tone on two pins at the other end. Which of the following faults have you discovered?

test_cases.solution: A short is when a wire is connected to two or more pins at one end of the cable or when the conductors of two or more wires are touching inside the cable. This would cause a tone applied to a single pin at one end to be heard on multiple pins at the other end. The other three options would not cause this to occur. An open circuit would manifest as a failure to detect a tone on a wire, indicating that there is either a break in the wire somewhere inside the cable or a bad connection with the pin in one or both connectors. A split pair is a connection in which two wires are incorrectly mapped in exactly the same way on both ends of the cable. Crosstalk is a type of interference caused by signals on one wire bleeding over to other wires

incident.title: Which of the following are true about IP address 172.16.99.45’s IP network? (Choose two answers.)
incident.question: Which of the following are true about IP address 172.16.99.45’s IP network? (Choose two answers.)
choices: The network is a Class B network.
The default mask for the network is 255.255.255.0.
The number of host bits in the unsubnetted network is 16.

test_cases.expected_root_cause: The network is a Class B network.; The number of host bits in the unsubnetted network is 16.
test_cases.solution: The first octet (172) is in the range of values for Class B addresses (128–191). As a result, the network ID can be formed by copying the first two octets (172.16) and writing 0s for the last two octets (172.16.0.0). The default mask for all Class B networks is 255.255.0.0, and the number of host bits in all unsubnetted Class B networks is 16
acceptable_answers: the network is a class b network.; the number of host bits in the unsubnetted network is 16.
